thread.title: Spotify Touted On Wall Street, Called Netflix For Music

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Spotify Touted On Wall Street, Called Netflix For Music
text:
Streaming music leader Spotify Technology ( SPOT ) received a bunch of bullish analyst calls on Monday ahead of its first quarterly report as a public company.
X At least six Wall Street firms initiated coverage of Spotify on Monday. Bank of America, Evercore ISI, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley and UBS all set buy ratings on the stock.
UBS was the most bullish, with a price target of 200. Bank of America initiated coverage at 195. Evercore ISI, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley started coverage with a price target of 190.
Spotify shares rose 1.8% to close at 165.26 . The company went public on April 3, starting at 165.90 and hit an all-time high of 169 the same day.
 Based in Stockholm, Spotify is scheduled to report first-quarter results after the market close on Wednesday. Analysts expect the company to lose 34 cents a share on revenue of $1.4 billion, according to Zacks Investment Research.
Largest Pure-Play Service Investor focus will be on subscriber growth. Spotify previously reported having 157 million monthly active users and 71 million paying subscribers for its premium service. It competes with Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ) unit Google, Pandora Media ( P ) and others in the subscription streaming music business.
JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth said the company will generate strong user growth over the next five years, which will drive its stock higher. He compared it to subscription streaming video leader Netflix ( NFLX ).
"Spotify is the largest pure-play music streaming service, and is both driving and benefiting from the ongoing secular shift from a 'transaction-based' model to an 'access-based' streaming model," Anmuth said in a note to clients. "We believe Netflix is the closest operating comp to Spotify, as both benefit from the secular shift to streaming through subscription-based models."
Spotify Seen Reaching 200 Million Subscribers Evercore ISI analyst Anthony DiClemente said Spotify will benefit from its market leading position. Thanks to a large subscriber base, it should be able to get favorable terms from music content owners, he said. It also could leverage its user base to generate "high-margin ancillary marketplace revenue streams," DiClemente said in a note to clients.
Spotify should be able to increase its premium users from 70 million to about 200 million by 2020, Morgan Stanley analyst Benjamin Swinburne said in a report.
Last week, though, it received a cautious report from B. Riley FBR analyst Barton Crockett. He initiated coverage at neutral with a 12-month price target of 156.
"We believe this company is well on its way to becoming a standard music utility of hundreds of millions of smartphones globally, gaining leverage over labels and musicians for rising margins and positive free cash flow," Crockett wrote. "But Spotify's growth has been paired with substantial discounting that we see as likely to continue, constraining the value of that subscriber growth."
